purpose: Atogepant is a daily pill used to help prevent migraines before they start. It is not used to treat a migraine that has already begun. Doctors prescribe it for adults who get migraines frequently and want to reduce how often they happen.
how_it_works: During a migraine, your body releases a protein called CGRP that causes pain and inflammation in the brain. Atogepant works by blocking the receptor that CGRP attaches to, so the signal that triggers a migraine gets interrupted. Think of it like putting a lock cover over a keyhole so the key cannot get in and start the pain process.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, constipation, tiredness, and decreased appetite. Some people may also notice stomach pain or feeling dizzy. These effects are usually mild and often get better as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have serious liver or kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Let your doctor and pharmacist know about all other medications you take, because some drugs can affect how atogepant works in your body. Do not take it if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant without talking to your doctor first. Avoid taking it with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors like certain antibiotics or antifungal medications unless your doctor says it is okay.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Your doctor may prescribe 10 mg, 30 mg, or 60 mg depending on your situation. Try to take it at the same time each day to keep it working consistently.
